content_sections.heading: DU LDE 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: This examination is meant for eligible existing employees of the University of Delhi. It is not an open competitive recruitment for outside applicants. Candidates should have 3 years of regular service as Section Officer/Private Secretary in Pay Level 7 or above. Selection is based on merit from among eligible feeder-cadre employees having the required experience, on the basis of written test, service record and interview. Candidates should have 3 years of regular service in the feeder grade of Senior Assistant/Legal Assistant in Pay Level 6. They should also have undergone one week of training in administrative and financial skills conducted by a College, University or another training institution. Eligible candidates include Assistants, Hindi Assistants, Assistant Archivists or incumbents of other ex-cadre posts working in Pay Level 5/Pay Level 4 with at least 3 years of regular service in the cadre. Junior Assistants/Hindi Typists working in Pay Level 2 with at least 3 years of regular service in the cadre are eligible. Group C employees working in Pay Level 1 who possess Senior Secondary (10+2) or equivalent qualification and have completed at least 3 years of regular service in the grade are eligible.

content_sections.heading: DU Limited Departmental Examination Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection for Assistant Registrar involves Written Test, Service Record and Interview/Personality Test. Paper I covers General Studies. Paper II covers University Administration, including University rules, statutes, ordinances, governance, examination regulations, recruitment rules, CCS rules, reservation rules, General Financial Rules, leave rules, Budget and Accounts, RTI Act and related administrative subjects. Service Record is based on ACR/APAR for the preceding three years. The Interview/Personality Test assesses academic qualifications, relevant experience, extra-curricular activities, general awareness, communication, problem-solving ability and overall personality. The test duration is 2 hours. The Senior Assistant departmental examination is also for 2 hours. The Assistant departmental examination has a duration of 2 hours. A qualifying on-spot typing test will be conducted on computer. The qualifying typing speed is 30 words per minute. PwBD candidates who are entitled to complete exemption from typing test under Central Government guidelines are exempt from the skill test. The question papers are bilingual in English and Hindi. Candidates may respond in either language, but the same medium must be used throughout the examination.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are available under Delhi University Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 130 vacancies have been announced for internal departmental promotion across Assistant Registrar, Section Officer, Senior Assistant, Assistant, and Junior Assistant posts.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for Delhi University Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date for the receipt of the online application is 28 October 2026, and the last date for the receipt of the hard copy of the application is 29 October 2026.

faq.question: Q3. Who is eligible to apply for these promotional posts?
faq.answer: Regular employees working in specified feeder cadres with the required minimum years of service (such as 3 years of regular service) are eligible to apply as per the post-wise criteria detailed in Annexure-I.

faq.question: Q4. Is there any application fee for Delhi University Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The notification does not mention any application fee for submitting the recruitment forms.

faq.question: Q5. How should the application be submitted?
faq.answer: Candidates must first submit the online application via the website du.ac.in, and then submit a signed hard copy of the application received via email, duly forwarded by the Head of the Branch, to the Office of the Deputy Registrar (R&P) by hand.

faq.question: Q6. What is the selection process for Junior Assistant posts?
faq.answer: The selection process for Junior Assistant includes a Written Test comprising Paper-I (MCQ Type) and Paper-II (Essay), followed by a skill test involving an on-spot typing test at a qualifying speed of 30 words per minute on a computer.

faq.question: Q7. Where should the hard copy of the application be submitted?
faq.answer: The hard copy must be submitted in the Office of the Deputy Registrar (R&P), Room No. 113, 1st Floor, New Administrative Block, University of Delhi.

faq.question: Q8. Are there category-wise vacancy reservations?
faq.answer: Yes, vacancies are categorized into UR, SC, ST, and horizontal reservations for PwBD candidates as specified in the official vacancy table.
